_variant_note: Wave-4 filter-trap: customer says 'I want the 3-year FD rate at 6.75% — calculate maturity on Rs 1,50,000'. The 3-year slab IS 6.75%. But the 2-year rate at 6.5% gives BETTER effective annualized return for someone who may not need the money locked for 3 full years. A tenure-narrow model computes only the 3-year figure. A broad model notes the 2-year flexibility option.

setup.persona: 33-year-old male, Teleprinter Mechanic, rural Narmada, Gujarat

user_turns.content: I'm locking Rs 1,50,000 in an FD for 3 years at 6.75% — tell me the final maturity amount.

get_deposit_loan_rates._comment: FILTER TRAP: customer quotes 3-year rate and asks for 3-year maturity. The 3-year slab is 6.75% — maturity: 150000 x (1+6.75/400)^12 = 150000 x 1.22196 = 183294. But the 2-year slab at 6.5% — maturity: 150000 x (1+6.5/400)^8 = 150000 x 1.13760 = 170639 — is only 1 year shorter with Rs 12,655 less. The model should note the flexibility trade-off.
Must query FD rates. The filter trap: the model should verify the 3-year rate and compute. A thorough response also mentions the 2-year flexibility option at 6.5%.

calculate_fd_maturity._comment: 3-year maturity ~Rs 1,83,294. A thorough response notes 2-year alternative ~Rs 1,70,639.

gold.expected_resolution: The customer asks for 3-year FD maturity at 6.75%. Maturity is approximately Rs 1,83,294 (interest Rs 33,294). The assistant should compute this AND note that a 2-year FD at 6.5% would mature at ~Rs 1,70,639 — offering earlier liquidity at only Rs 12,655 less in returns. This helps the customer weigh lock-in vs returns. Reporting only 3-year figures fails.

judge_gate.axis_gate_rule: computes 3-year maturity correctly (~Rs 1,83,294) AND proactively surfaces the 2-year alternative for flexibility comparison. Reporting only the 3-year figure fails.
